Discretized and rounded distributions

Source: R/operators.R
discretize.Rd

discretize() turns a continuous law into a discrete one on the integers by interval probabilities P(Y = k) = F(k + 1 - offset) - F(k - offset) (the default offset = 0 maps [k, k + 1) to k; offset = 0.5 rounds to the nearest integer). round_dist() gives the law of a value rounded to digits decimals, P(Y = y) = F(y + h/2) - F(y - h/2) with h = 10^-digits, on the grid of multiples of h.

Usage

discretize(base, offset = 0)

round_dist(base, digits = 0)

Arguments

base

Continuous base family.

offset

Shift of the interval boundaries.

digits

Number of decimals.

Value

A regcomp_family.

Examples

dg <- discretize("gamma")
d <- distribution(dg, mu = 3, sigma = 0.5)
sum(prob(d, 0:200))
#> [1] 1
r1 <- round_dist("normal", digits = 1)
